To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rise in the employee share of employment is a key determinant of the rise of the modern income tax.
the rise in the share of employees is the main driver of the rise in the tax capacity, and that the rise in tax capacity in turn is the main driver in the rise in income inequality.

(1) within country the share of employees in total employment rises over the income distribution and increases at all income levels as countries develop, (2) the income level covered by the tax exemption threshold moves downward as countries develop and tracks the increase in employee shares, (3) movements in tax exemption thresholds explain the variation in tax revenue observed across development, and (4) the increase in employee share leads to an expansion in the income tax base and increase in tax revenue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the employment structure of an economy affects its ability to raise tax revenues, and how the ability to raise tax revenue affects the employment structure of the economy.
the role of the modern tax system in economic development.
the rise of modern tax systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rise in the employee share over the long run is an important driver of the rise of the income tax.
the rise of employee shares in the labor force over the course of development drives growth in income taxation.
the rise of the modern tax system is driven by the rise of the employee share.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a rise in employee share explains a large fraction of the rise in tax collection over the development process.
the rise of employee jobs is a key driver of the rise of the income tax system.
employee share is an important driver of tax capacity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rise in the employee share is the key driver of the rise of the modern tax system.
a high share of employees is a necessary condition to sustain the growth of the income tax capacity, and the rise of the employee share over time explains the expansion of the tax base.
the transition from self to employee employment is an important determinant of the rise of the modern tax system, and a necessary condition for the expansion of income tax revenue.
